title: Profile Before You Plot
objective: After this lesson you will be able to profile any dataset (shapes, types, missingness, distributions, outliers) and state what each finding implies for chart choice — before drawing a single chart.
why: Charts drawn on unprofiled data visualize assumptions: string prices, missing months, outlier-dominated scales, single-category 'comparisons'. Profiling (ten minutes: shapes, dtypes, nulls, ranges, value counts) determines what can honestly be shown — chart choice follows data reality, never precedes it.

blocks.text: **Shape** (rows × columns vs source claims — row loss detected here), **types** (parsed as intended?), **missingness** (per-column rates + patterns: random vs structural), **ranges** (min/max exposing negatives, futures, impossibles), **value counts** (single-category comparisons and dominant classes caught early). Each finding constrains chart choice downstream.

blocks.caption: Profile output feeds chart choice and cleaning queues alike

blocks.text: Extreme values are guilty until proven data-entry: $1M order (whale or typo?), year-2099 timestamps (default-fill bugs?), 200-character names (concatenation errors). Rule: investigate each extreme (source check), then **cap, flag, or exclude with note** — never silently drop (dropped extremes bias means) nor blindly keep (one whale rescales every axis).

blocks.title: Profile output is a deliverable
blocks.text: Save the profile (shapes, nulls, ranges, value counts) as the dataset's dossier section — downstream chart choices cite it, cleaning queues consume it, and reviewers audit against it. Profiling unwritten never happened.

blocks.title: Profile the orders
blocks.note: Run it: 4×3 shape, 1 missing total, max 99999 flagged for investigation. Profile outputs route work: missingness to cleaning, extremes to investigation, shapes to chart choice.

items: Profile quartet + outliers before any chart: shapes, types, missingness, ranges, value counts
Outliers investigated (source check) then capped/flagged/excluded-with-note — never silent either way
Every finding routes somewhere: chart choice, cleaning queue, or investigation

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice profiler and map each output to its route (chart/clean/investigate). (b) Decide the 99999 and null-total rows (investigate? cap? quarantine?) with one-line reasons. (c) State what single-category value-counts would do to a comparison chart.
hints: Outputs: 4×3 shape, total missing 1 (cleaning), max 99999 (investigate: whale vs typo).
99999: investigate source first (whale→cap+flag, typo→quarantine); null total: quarantine (money needs truth).
Single category: comparison with one bar — vacuous; pivot to distribution-over-time or drop the chart.
exercise.why: Finding-to-route mapping (profile outputs drive chart/clean/investigate), disposition judgment (whale vs typo handling), and vacuity detection (single-category comparisons) are the three profiling disciplines.
exercise.code: // Profile-route pattern: every finding maps to chart, cleaning, or investigation.

quiz.q: One $99999 order among $100s. Chart it raw?
options: Investigate first (whale vs typo), then cap/flag/exclude-with-note — raw extremes rescale everything silently
quiz.explain: Extremes need source verdicts before rendering decisions. Uninvestigated outliers corrupt scales and means alike.

quiz.q: Null totals in 20% of rows. Handling?
options: Quarantine with reasons (money needs truth) + report the rate — zeros fabricate revenue, drops need justification
quiz.explain: Missing money is a data-quality finding with a rate attached, not a fill-in-the-blank. Quarantine preserves truth.

quiz.q: Value counts show one category only. Comparison chart?
options: Vacuous — change the question (distribution over time?) or drop it; one bar compares nothing
quiz.explain: Comparisons need ≥2 groups by definition. Single-category data asks different questions — pivot, don't decorate.

summary: Profile quartet + outliers with routes: chart, clean, or investigate. Chart choice follows data reality — established here, assumed everywhere after.
next: Reality established — now match questions to charts: the selection matrix. Next: chart choice by question.
